reviews.title: Phenomenal app
reviews.text: I’ve had the app for months now. The free version is great, but it’s worth the $40 a year for the full version. In my lifetime I’ve bought so many supplements based on word of mouth, snake-oil advertising and mostly just guessing. With this app I’ve found some of my supplements were garbage and have saved money buying exactly what I need. I wouldn’t buy any supplement without this app. There are so many great features I can’t list them all. Get the app unless you want to spend a fortune on low-rated poor quality supplements.

reviews.title: Don’t even sample a single supplement without consulting this app
reviews.text: I’ve been using supplements for years trusting a family member and chemist to study the aspects in this app independently which is a lot of work. So many supplement companies sponsor the studies on their own products so some results cannot be trusted. This app is based on independent research that actually can be trusted and shows the values on multiple aspects of the supplement itself and the brand. I’m simply never not using this info to stay informed about the value and safety of my health supplements. There are many other offerings through the app I have not tried but would consider at some point. There is so much value in the free version alone!

reviews.title: Indispensable
reviews.text: I figured the price was reasonable enough just for my supplement stack analysis. Little did I know that I’d be jumping onto this thing every time I considered a new addition to my stack. It also offers the most reliable available information on the quality and veracity of any supplement source or brand. The lack of FDA oversight for the supplement industry has always seemed like a deficit, but who wants the government involved in personal choices when you’ve got a resource like this? Pounce.

reviews.title: Not Trustworthy
reviews.text:
Purchased SuppCo Pro.  Many of the supplements that I was taking had not been rated.  Also, I noted that the highest rated supplements were by far the most expensive—suspicious, but as they weigh third party testing highly, I gave them the benefit of the doubt.  

Soon, I received a notice that I was invited to the “buyers club.”  Here I could purchase the most highly rated supplements and receive 30% credit for subsequent purchases.

Sounds good right?  Wrong, now SuppCo profits directly from sales.  I enquired and the assured me they did not.  I was born at night, but not last night.

More of the same, another supplement SCAM.
